responses.question_text: Do you encrypt data at rest using AES-256 or equivalent?
responses.response_text: Yes. All data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 encryption across all storage systems, including databases, file stores, and backups [soc2_report.pdf:page_12].

responses.question_text: Do you encrypt data in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher?
responses.response_text: Yes. All data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.3. Legacy TLS versions below 1.2 are disabled at the load balancer level [soc2_report.pdf:page_13].

responses.question_text: Describe your data classification policy.
responses.response_text: Tracelight maintains a four-tier data classification framework: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. All customer financial model data is classified as Restricted and subject to the highest level of access controls and encryption requirements [security_policy.pdf:page_4]. Classification is enforced programmatically via automated tagging in our CI/CD pipeline.

responses.question_text: Do you maintain a zero data retention policy for customer data after processing?
responses.response_text: Yes. Tracelight operates a zero-retention architecture. Customer spreadsheet data is processed ephemerally in memory and is never written to persistent storage. This is validated quarterly by our external auditors [soc2_report.pdf:page_18].

responses.question_text: Do you implement data loss prevention (DLP) controls?
responses.response_text: Yes. DLP controls are implemented at the endpoint, network, and application layers [REQUIRES REVIEW — INSUFFICIENT KB COVERAGE]. We monitor for unauthorized data exfiltration via our SIEM integration.

responses.question_text: Do you enforce multi-factor authentication for all user accounts?
responses.response_text: Yes. MFA is enforced for all employees, contractors, and administrative access to production systems. We use hardware security keys (FIDO2) as the primary second factor [security_policy.pdf:page_7].

responses.question_text: Describe your role-based access control (RBAC) implementation.
responses.response_text: Tracelight implements RBAC across all production systems using a principle of least privilege model. Roles are defined per service and reviewed quarterly by the engineering leads. Access grants require manager approval and are logged in our IAM system [security_policy.pdf:page_8]. Privileged access to production databases requires additional just-in-time approval via our PAM solution.

responses.question_text: Do you conduct periodic access reviews?
responses.response_text: Yes. Access reviews are conducted quarterly for all systems and monthly for privileged accounts. Stale accounts are automatically disabled after 90 days of inactivity [soc2_report.pdf:page_22].

responses.question_text: Describe your third-party vendor access management process.
responses.response_text: Third-party vendors are granted access on a time-limited, project-scoped basis only. All vendor access is provisioned through a dedicated VPN segment with network segmentation [REQUIRES REVIEW — INSUFFICIENT KB COVERAGE].

responses.question_text: Do you maintain a business continuity plan (BCP)?
responses.response_text: Yes. Tracelight maintains a comprehensive BCP that is tested annually via tabletop exercises and bi-annually via failover drills. RTO is 4 hours and RPO is 1 hour for all critical systems [incident_response.pdf:page_3].

responses.question_text: Describe your disaster recovery architecture.
responses.response_text: Our production infrastructure runs on AWS across two availability zones (eu-west-1a, eu-west-1b) with automated failover. Database replication is synchronous with a standby in a third AZ. Full infrastructure can be reprovisioned from IaC templates in under 2 hours [incident_response.pdf:page_5]. Backups are replicated to a separate AWS region (eu-central-1) for geographic redundancy.

responses.question_text: When was your BCP last tested?
responses.response_text: The most recent full BCP test was conducted in Q4 2025. A tabletop exercise simulating a ransomware scenario was completed in January 2026 [incident_response.pdf:page_8].

responses.question_text: Describe your incident response plan.
responses.response_text: Tracelight operates a four-phase incident response framework: Detection, Containment, Eradication, and Recovery. The IRP is maintained by the CTO and reviewed quarterly. All incidents are classified by severity (P1-P4) with defined escalation paths and SLAs [incident_response.pdf:page_2]. P1 incidents trigger immediate notification to the founding team and affected customers within 24 hours.

responses.question_text: Have you experienced any security breaches in the last 24 months?
responses.response_text: No. Tracelight has not experienced any security breaches, data leaks, or unauthorized access incidents in the 24-month period ending March 2026. This is confirmed in our SOC 2 Type II report [soc2_report.pdf:page_31].

responses.question_text: Do you maintain 24/7 security monitoring?
responses.response_text: Yes. We operate continuous security monitoring via a managed SIEM solution with 24/7 alerting. Critical alerts page the on-call engineer within 5 minutes [REQUIRES REVIEW — INSUFFICIENT KB COVERAGE].

responses.question_text: Do you use a cloud service provider that maintains SOC 2 Type II certification?
responses.response_text: Yes. Tracelight is hosted on AWS, which maintains SOC 2 Type II certification, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS compliance. AWS compliance reports are available via AWS Artifact [soc2_report.pdf:page_6].

responses.question_text: Describe your container security practices.
responses.response_text: All containers run on hardened, minimal base images (distroless) scanned in CI via Trivy. Runtime monitoring is provided by Falco. Container images are signed and stored in a private ECR registry with immutable tags [security_policy.pdf:page_15].

responses.question_text: Do you enforce least-privilege access for cloud IAM roles?
responses.response_text: Yes. All AWS IAM roles follow least-privilege principles. Policies are defined in Terraform and reviewed in PR. No wildcard (*) actions are permitted in production accounts [security_policy.pdf:page_10].

responses.question_text: Do you maintain SOC 2 Type II certification?
responses.response_text: Yes. Tracelight achieved SOC 2 Type II certification in 2025, covering the Trust Service Criteria of Security, Availability, and Confidentiality. The audit period covers January-December 2025 [soc2_report.pdf:page_1].

responses.question_text: Describe your approach to GDPR compliance for EU customer data.
responses.response_text: Tracelight processes customer data as a data processor under GDPR. Our zero-retention architecture means no personal data is stored post-processing. We maintain a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) template compliant with Standard Contractual Clauses [REQUIRES REVIEW — INSUFFICIENT KB COVERAGE]. Our DPO can be contacted at privacy@tracelight.ai.
